author: Codex socialist_green assessment agent (AI-assisted independent assessment)
changeNote: Completed 240 individually interpreted responses and separate substantive evidence review. User authorised neutral representative doctrinal modelling; no 12Axes answers or scores imported.

metadata.name: Social Democracy
metadata.description: Reformist social democracy combining competitive democracy, a mixed economy, labour rights and inclusive social provision.
metadata.period: Post-war European reformism; 1989 principles with 2026 policy context
metadata.scope: Reformist parliamentary social democracy, combining a mixed economy, universal social provision and labour rights. The Socialist International declaration includes democratic-socialist aspirations; this profile selects its explicit mixed-economy formulation rather than assuming total social ownership. This is a representative interpretation, not a questionnaire submitted by adherents. Numeric neutral means a stated mixed/conditional judgement, including rejection of the premise where explained; it is not a claim of measured empirical equivalence. Modern biological and technology items are conditional interpretive judgements where no exact historical position exists; they must not be read as empirical findings or a representative survey of adherents.
metadata.phrase: A democratic society combining a regulated market economy with social insurance, labour rights and redistribution.

sources.title: Declaration of principles, Stockholm June 1989 (day not supplied)
Socialism, especially ownership, Marxist phases and human nature
Transfer of Govia Thameslink Railway’s services into public ownership

axes.brief: SI paragraphs 17–27 make competitive elections, pluralism, independent courts and rights substantive ends.
axes.counterEvidence: Participation does not specify a referendum for every law; recall answers are inferred, not directly prescribed.

answers.rationale: Competitive elections are explicitly indispensable to political democracy.
Popular choice cannot be replaced by expert appointment.
Equal citizenship excludes educational voting tests.
Parliamentary consent constrains executive lawmaking.
Pluralist elections require equal opposition opportunity.
Democratic accountability requires scrutiny of expenditure.
An independent judiciary is explicitly part of SI democracy.
Union participation does not replace universal electoral choice.
Incumbents cannot monopolise permissible electoral opinion.
Direct participation can supplement parliamentary representation under rights safeguards.
Collective democratic decision-making rejects personal supremacy.
Defined removal safeguards democratic responsibility.
Unilateral postponement undermines free electoral choice.
Recall can strengthen accountability when procedure protects fair participation.
Government must remain accountable to the electorate.
Military judgement cannot supplant civilian democratic choice.

axes.brief: SI civil rights protect expression, association and privacy; democratically accountable public safety remains legitimate.
axes.counterEvidence: Freedom is not absolute immunity from preventing harm. Self-regarding health mandates are distinct from protection of others.

answers.rationale: Personal autonomy favours harm-reduction over punishment for self-regarding choices.
Judicial oversight can reconcile crime investigation with privacy.
Collective action requires room for peaceful disruptive protest.
Free expression protects criticism of institutions.
Health solidarity supports prevention but self-regarding compulsion requires justification.
Indiscriminate long retention undermines basic privacy.
Proportionate road-safety checks protect others from harm.
Judicial safeguards matter but restrictions before offending remain exceptional.
Pluralism precludes censorship based merely on moral disapproval.
Anonymous communication protects association and expression.
Broad suspicionless searches risk unequal and arbitrary treatment.
Concrete danger permits limits but peaceful assembly requires narrow tailoring.
Independent warrants protect homes from arbitrary intrusion.
Exposing official misconduct serves democratic accountability.
Public safety supports stronger controls than a violence-history check alone.
Court-free indefinite detention contradicts protected civil rights.

axes.brief: SI paragraph 66 explicitly favours multicultural coexistence while maintaining common citizenship.
axes.counterEvidence: Cultural equality does not automatically privilege a minority practice over every common public rule.

answers.rationale: Cultural uniformity conflicts with explicitly valued diversity.
Equal participation can require publicly funded accommodation.
Civic integration does not require adoption of every majority custom.
Multiple identities are compatible with citizenship.
Common communication and minority access both need provision.
Equal recognition includes Indigenous communities.
Cultural equality opposes reserving support primarily for predominant traditions.
Neither community preference nor majority culture overrides equal individual rights automatically.
Reasonable accommodation is preferable to rigid uniform calendars.
Multicultural national identity is explicitly compatible with SI values.
Shared participation can coexist with distinct cultural communities.
Translation where useful advances access and participation.
Shared citizenship and community heritage need not be ranked universally.
Religious accommodation matters but differential clothing exceptions need a concrete justification.
Cultural diversity is treated as enriching common society.
Integration should enable participation without forced abandonment of customs.

axes.brief: Universal dignity and migrant equality support accessible migration, qualified by democratic management and social capacity.
axes.counterEvidence: The declaration is not a detailed immigration code. Conditional answers balance stated international solidarity with social provision, not invented numerical quotas.

answers.rationale: Social capacity matters but rigid caps can conflict with humanitarian obligations.
Improving life is a legitimate reason for migration under fair rules.
Skills-only selection excludes family and humanitarian duties.
Family unity supports admission of dependants.
Refugees deserve protection irrespective of cultural fit or economic skills.
Regularisation and fair-process removal depend on circumstances rather than automatic outcomes.
Labour demand matters alongside housing, wages and solidarity.
Capacity pressure calls for investment as well as possible temporary moderation.
Family unity merits protection from a rigid uniform quota.
Employment normally supports lawful labour admission.
Independent humanitarian and personal routes should remain available.
A degree is a relevant connection but neither a complete entitlement nor irrelevant.
Persecution protection should survive ordinary admission caps.
Equal dignity opposes preference by cultural origin.
Social inclusion extends welfare protections to resident migrants.
Diversity is welcome but admission should not prefer difference for its own sake.

axes.brief: SI peace and disarmament commitments favour diplomacy without making abandonment of defensive protection obligatory.
axes.counterEvidence: Disarmament is a central objective, but the declaration also contemplates defensive systems and collective security.

answers.rationale: National advantage alone cannot justify initiating force.
Peaceful negotiation is central even when slower.
Arms competition diverts resources and undermines shared security.
Imminence may justify defence but evidence and alternatives require exceptional scrutiny.
Defensive use is preferred while collective protection remains a qualification.
Compulsory male-only service is not the preferred foundation of security.
Serious concessions can be justified to preserve peace.
Unsupervised lethal targeting conflicts with human responsibility.
Defence rather than expeditionary ambition fits common security.
Peace commitments do not necessarily require abandoning attacked allies.
Prolonged overseas war capacity is lower priority than common defence.
A territorial claim should not trigger a chosen war.
Negotiated settlement is preferable to coercive military bargaining.
War prevention normally outweighs demonstrations of resolve.
Defensive intelligence can be justified but escalatory espionage has costs.
Negotiated disarmament is an explicit SI objective.

axes.brief: SI global cooperation and reformed multilateral bodies qualify sovereign discretion.
axes.counterEvidence: The declaration recognises national self-government; internationalism is conditional on democratic and equitable institutions.

answers.rationale: Democratic multilateral obligations can qualify national legal supremacy.
Legitimately agreed institutions may bind dissenting governments.
International adjudication must have effect if commitments are meaningful.
Durable cooperation can warrant restrictions on unilateral action.
National self-government coexists with binding agreed obligations.
International legal accountability protects common rights.
Global solidarity can outweigh immediate national interest.
Cross-border ecology calls for binding international coordination.
Common foreign-policy cooperation is compatible with international solidarity.
International human rights should constrain domestic legislation.
Shared monetary authority can aid cooperation but must permit democratic social policy.
Pooled resources are central to common international problems.
Shared migration responsibility can justify pooled border authority.
Common trade rules are preferable when democratic and socially accountable.
A democratic federation is possible but the declaration preserves multiple institutional routes.
Enforcing agreed rights and rules can justify foregoing short-term advantage.

axes.brief: SI paragraphs 59–64 combine public enterprises, cooperatives and private markets, with democratic control determined by social function.
axes.counterEvidence: The UK Department for Transport confirms the 31 May 2026 GTR transfer under the public-ownership Act. This is a recent sector-specific implementation, not evidence that every industry should be nationalised.

answers.rationale: A mixed economy retains extensive private business alongside social and public enterprise.
Essential networks justify accountable public ownership.
Ownership choice should reflect democratic control as well as comparable service metrics.
Public enterprise can further social priorities even in competitive sectors.
Publicly accountable healthcare facilities better secure a universal service mission.
Rail infrastructure is a suitable publicly owned network under mixed-economy reasoning; the cited 2026 transfer concerns operations, not a change in infrastructure ownership.
Lower cost matters but continuity and public accountability can justify direct provision.
Public banking can support investment alongside private credit.
Social-purpose holdings should not routinely be privatised.
Public housing can materially broaden affordable access.
Regulation sometimes suffices but strategic public control may also be warranted.
Public resource ownership can distribute common-resource benefits.
Contracting depends on accountability and labour standards, not ownership presumption.
Strategic purpose can outweigh one-off sale proceeds.
Repeated subsidy warrants investigation, not automatic privatisation of a social service.
A public broadcaster can support accessible democratic information.

axes.brief: SI supports accountable international competition and development rather than either blanket protection or unregulated trade.
axes.counterEvidence: Global South development and labour rights qualify market openness. Protection is assessed by purpose rather than assumed from the socialist label.

answers.rationale: Protection is justified by social needs rather than domestic status alone.
International competition can be beneficial with adjustment support.
Social and environmental procurement can justify preference but mere nationality is insufficient.
Sourcing is normally free within labour and environmental rules.
Essential resilience can justify selective measures, not blanket import suppression.
Reciprocal rules and development needs complicate unilateral liberalisation.
Temporary infant-industry support can assist development.
Equal ordinary investment access is compatible with regulation.
Food security can justify safeguards but consumer costs and foreign farmers matter.
Adjustment support is generally preferable to permanent barriers.
Retaliation may enforce rules but escalation can harm workers everywhere.
Equal product taxation generally supports fair competition.
Subsidy-related restrictions can prevent destructive unfair competition.
Lower tariffs and supply security should be considered jointly.
Strategic public control can justify screening foreign acquisition.
Access to cross-border services is desirable subject to ordinary regulation.

axes.brief: SI accepts market signals within public investment, labour protection and democratic economic policy.
axes.counterEvidence: The declaration explicitly values markets and rejects state ownership as a universal remedy; it does not endorse a command economy.

answers.rationale: Market firms normally choose output within social regulation.
Routine compulsory output targets are not the mixed-economy norm.
Markets provide useful ordinary price signals.
Public investment strategy can direct development toward shared priorities.
Demand matters but employment and social needs can justify intervention.
Essential affordability can justify carefully designed price controls.
Ordinary entry should not require proving a national production need.
Public credit policy can direct investment toward social priorities.
Ordinary mobility is useful but destabilising capital flows may warrant controls.
Selected subsidies can implement democratically chosen development priorities.
Accountable public monetary institutions are preferred to competing private money.
A wage floor protects workers’ social rights.
Negotiation through strong unions is preferable to comprehensive wage schedules.
Monetary policy should consider employment and democratic economic goals.
Tenant security and affordability can justify rent regulation.
Macroeconomic coordination is appropriate but ordinary output remains partly decentralised.

axes.brief: Social citizenship and material equality require substantial redistributive taxation and inclusive income security.
axes.counterEvidence: Equal opportunity and social participation need not imply identical outcomes or denial of work incentives.

answers.rationale: Reducing material inequality is a core distributive goal.
Income inequality is itself a legitimate reason for progressive fiscal action.
Adequate social minimums justify shared tax costs.
Social citizenship exceeds a subsistence-only safety net.
Ability to pay supports strongly progressive income tax.
Fair contribution usually outweighs marginal retention by the better-off.
Inheritance taxation can counter entrenched unequal opportunity.
Ongoing need should not be cut off by arbitrary benefit expiry.
Wealth-based transfers can reduce entrenched inequality.
Benefits should meet social need rather than be kept low for taxpayers.
Participation in ordinary social life is a substantive social right.
Tax cuts should not generally outrank improving inadequate support.
Supplements can improve living standards for low-paid workers.
Progressive marginal rates reflect different capacity to contribute.
Compensated land reform can broaden opportunity in unequal agrarian settings.
Inclusive social provision should extend beyond households facing bare destitution.

axes.brief: SI pluralism protects belief while equal citizenship prevents clerical political privilege.
axes.counterEvidence: The movement includes religious and secular humanist traditions. Private religious identity is not governmental religious authority.

answers.rationale: Shared civil reasons allow equal treatment across faiths.
No particular creed should be an official legal source.
Democratic government must be independent of clerical approval.
Constitutional privilege for one faith weakens equal citizenship.
Teaching about religions can respect freedom of conscience.
State schools should not cultivate a preferred official belief.
Elected civil law must govern state courts.
Clerical office does not warrant privileged review of legislation.
Inclusive ceremonies should avoid official religious endorsement.
Public funds should serve common purposes rather than strengthen a creed.
Religious neutrality protects equal civic belonging.
Common inherited holidays can remain but explicit endorsement of one religion is problematic.
Religious office should not itself confer political office.
Religious organisations should normally use the same charitable rules as others.
Civil marriage must be available independently of faith approval.
Voluntary religious practice cannot displace equal civil family rights.

axes.brief: SI gender equality and opposition to patriarchy support changing restrictive social roles; modern applications are explicit inferences.
axes.counterEvidence: The declaration supports women’s emancipation but does not directly enumerate all modern LGBT policies; these are modest applications of equal citizenship.

answers.rationale: Social arrangements should change when equality and lived values warrant it.
Tradition alone should not override legitimate reform.
Equal dignity extends recognition beyond one household form.
Sex equality opposes compulsory traditional roles.
Equal civic treatment supports same-sex marriage as a modern inference.
Support for families should not impose one privileged model.
Reproductive agency supports acceptance of early abortion.
Universal education and children’s rights constrain a parental veto.
Equal treatment supports assessment by parenting capacity rather than sex.
Modesty customs should not determine everyone’s public dress.
Respectful language can adapt to personal identification.
Moral teaching should critically assess inherited norms.
Equal opportunity supports people entering nontraditional roles.
Durable reform benefits from deliberation but popularity and urgency can justify speed.
Inclusive education supports learning about diverse identities.
Cultural continuity has value without a presumption that every obsolete custom must persist.

axes.brief: SI paragraphs 44–53 combine useful technology with ecological protection and democratic safety assessment.
axes.counterEvidence: The declaration is favourable to technology that reduces drudgery; its cautions are about control, risk and exploitation.

answers.rationale: Useful innovation and democratic risk assessment must both be satisfied.
Significant unresolved long-term risks justify phased testing.
Public benefit and ecological loss require case-specific assessment.
Medical safety merits substantial study before general exposure.
Labour-saving technology can be beneficial when workers share gains and receive support.
Habitat protection and essential development both carry social value.
Food innovation requires environmental assessment rather than automatic rejection or adoption.
Nontherapeutic implants justify precaution given irreversible bodily effects.
Unproven technology should not displace proven consumption and efficiency measures.
Environmental uncertainty warrants review before irreversible construction.
Basic safety is insufficient where long-term neural harms remain unclear.
Evidence across patient groups is necessary for equitable medical safety.
The SI warning about genetic manipulation supports caution toward enhancement trials.
Ecological uncertainty justifies long-term crop safety evidence.
Housing need matters but land conservation remains a real constraint.
Irreversible harm warrants a strong precautionary threshold.

axes.brief: SI decentralised participation coexists with equal national social entitlements and international cooperation.
axes.counterEvidence: Local self-government cannot automatically justify unequal basic rights or national tax competition.

answers.rationale: Decentralised democratic participation deserves protected competence.
National solidarity and constitutional regional competence require negotiated allocation.
Self-determination matters but minority rights and shared obligations qualify separation.
Equal national entitlements can justify overriding local obstruction.
Regional institutions can vary within shared rights.
Democratic local accountability favours distributed policing with coordination.
National redistribution requires sharing revenue across unequal regions.
Common educational rights can coexist with regional curricular choices.
Some tax autonomy supports local accountability within equalisation.
National labour minimums prevent competition through weakened worker rights.
Local democratic choice should shape councils within general safeguards.
Equal healthcare entitlements support national coverage standards.
Indigenous cultural and civic equality supports local self-government.
Coordinated tax limits protect redistributive capacity.
Locally confined land decisions should generally be decentralised.
Multi-region emergencies justify national coordination with local participation.

axes.brief: SI treats education, class and discrimination as substantial influences, while explicitly recognising physical and mental differences.
axes.counterEvidence: Compensation for physical and mental inequalities is counter-evidence to a blank-slate reading. Fine biological comparisons receive a mixed judgement, not invented heritability estimates.

answers.rationale: Education and social conditions have a prominent causal role in the SI account.

The programme stresses unequal educational opportunity, while individual capacities also vary; these commitments do not establish a majority causal share for either inheritance or upbringing in country IQ differences.
SI identifies patriarchal social arrangements as a major source of gender behaviour.
Physical differences and life experience both matter; no universal stress ranking follows.
Opportunities and education strongly shape realised interests.
Both personal dispositions and learning can influence risk appetite.
Cooperative institutions and social learning cultivate solidarity.
Empathy is socially developed without denying individual biological differences.
Educational circumstances matter alongside recognised cognitive differences.
Moral education and social experience challenge biological primacy in moral reaction.
Social experience shapes which situations and groups seem threatening.
Temperament and formative experience interact rather than one being doctrinally dominant.
Cultural ideals and bodily responses both plausibly shape attraction.
The programme explains violence through social exclusion and oppressive institutions, supporting a modest structural inference rather than a claim that equal rights prove a biological finding.
Educational development contradicts explanations by inherited racial self-control.

The SI identifies sex discrimination, occupational inequality and unequal family responsibilities, favouring social explanations over differences in productive economic contribution as the main account of the pay gap.

review.notes: Read all 240 answers against the current question wording and checked values, rationales, cited source IDs and axis distinctions. Checked the SI declaration against SEP/IEP accounts and the government rail statement. The 31 May 2026 GTR transfer concerns operating services, not transfer of rail infrastructure; corrected source publication date to 1 June 2026. Reduced the overstrong racial-violence inference and clarified its structural rather than moral-equality basis. Culture16 is supported by the SI discussion of occupational subordination and family responsibilities. All answers remain labelled inferred: these are scoped representative models, not claimed questionnaire responses or empirical measurements of adherents. Review used no target scores or similarity tuning. Similarity audit remains the catalogue coordinator’s separate step.
